content:
Republican former House Speaker Newt Gingrich has joined a chorus of bipartisan critics condemning the return of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned earlier this month amid revelations he had an extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

Huang’s reinstatement Monday at the urging of President Donald Trump prompted a fiery X post on Monday from Gingrich.

“There is something profoundly wrong about Jensen Huang having a relationship with a Chinese Communist Spy and helping China get a huge number of very advanced computer chips when that was specifically against the policy of the United States Government and now he is being reinstated as ceo of the most advanced chip making company in the world,” Gingrich wrote.

Gingrich has been a longtime supporter of Trump and written several books about his presidency, but appeared to urge Democrats — who will take control of the House and Senate next year — to investigate the scandal.

“Congress should really dig into this as a national security issue of enormous proportions and also a significant failure in the federal bureaucracy,” he said.

Gingrich isn’t the only right-wing commentator or conservative lawmaker to decry Huang’s return. Rep. Michael McCaul (R-Texas) demanded on social media Monday that the Trump administration release evidence that Huang’s affair and business deals with an alleged spy are not a cause for concern.

Officials should explain to Congress and the public why “Mr. Huang’s extramarital relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset — along with Nvidia’s deeply concerning sales of advanced chips to Megaspeed — no longer poses a national security threat,” wrote McCaul.

Trump has publicly cast doubt on the national security risks and questioned whether Huang’s mistress is a spy. The president took credit on Monday for the Nvidia CEO’s reinstatement, telling CNBC about his conversations with the Nvidia board.

“I spoke to them, let me put it that way. And I convinced them,” he said.
